title: Weekly play
hookLine: play is practice too; David dances before the ark with all his might and tells Michal he will play before the LORD
tomorrow: a monk spread 150 psalms across a week. why not one day?

lines: DAVID DANCES WITH ALL HIS MIGHT.
cards: When did you last do something only because it was fun? Not useful fun. Just fun.

King David once did it in front of a whole city. The ark of God is coming up into Jerusalem with shouting and the sound of the trumpet, and David dances before it with all his might, girded with a linen ephod, leaping.
His wife Michal watches from a window, and the text says she despised him in her heart.

teach.h: THEREFORE WILL I PLAY BEFORE THE LORD.
teach.b: She meets him at the door. How glorious was the king today, she says, uncovering himself like a fool in front of the servant girls.
And David answers: it was before the LORD, "therefore will I play before the LORD." He doesn't apologize. He says he'll be even less dignified than that.
David's answer carries a teaching: in the Hebrew Bible, joy before God is worship, and it uses the body, not only the mind.

teach.h: PRAISE HIM WITH THE TIMBREL AND DANCE.
teach.b: The last psalm calls for it: "Praise him with the timbrel and dance." Jewish life keeps that alive.

teach.h: SIMCHAT TORAH: DANCING WITH THE SCROLLS.
teach.b: On Simchat Torah, the day the cycle of Torah readings ends and starts again from the beginning, people carry the scrolls around the synagogue and dance with them, circle after circle, children on shoulders, nobody grading the steps.
Joy isn't the opposite of holiness there. It's one of its shapes.
So weekly play isn't a break from practice. In David's story it can be practice. The part of you that worries how it looks gets set down for a while, the way David set down the king.
Play is the self that forgets it's being watched. That's why it belongs on the calendar, beside the silence and the study, and why it's fine to be bad at it.

how: On Simchat Torah, Jewish congregations carry the Torah scrolls around the synagogue in circles of singing and dancing; people who keep a weekly play hour often choose a game, a dance class, music or a sport done for its own sake.

o: a weekly sports league with points and wins
an hour a week of something done for joy
time to rest by watching something easy

games.q: David before the ark: tap the pairs.

s: David apologized to Michal for his dancing
he said he would play before the LORD, and be less dignified still.
in the Hebrew Bible, dance can be praise
Psalm 150: praise him with the timbrel and dance.
in the story, everyone agreed the dancing was beneath a king
Michal thought so; David answered that it was before the LORD.

games.q: at a friend's Jewish wedding the circle dancing starts, and you feel too awkward to join. what fits David's story?
o: join in: in David's story, joy before God isn't measured by how it looks.
stay seated: a holy celebration is only for people who know the steps.
wait until you've learned the steps properly, then join next time.
games.why: David danced with all his might and refused to be embarrassed. in his story, joy with the whole body is worship, not a performance.

practice: Stand up and move for a minute in a way that feels a little silly: sway, tap a rhythm on your legs, step side to side to a song in your head. Let it be unimpressive.
Then sit, feel your heartbeat, and choose one hour of play for this week.

wordCard.voice: Weekly play: an hour each week of doing something for joy, the way David played before the LORD, without checking who's at the window.

orig.note: Hebrew, 2 Samuel 6:21: and I will play. David's own word for his dancing before the LORD.

carryVoice: Here's the line: play. David danced with all his might, and he didn't apologize to anyone. That's today.
